title: Herding · dogs that move a flock
blurb: The working dogs of the sheep hill and the cattle yard: they gather, drive and hold stock, and most of them still need a job to be calm.

items.d: The sheepdog of the Anglo-Scottish border: black and white, tireless, and the standard for herding trials.
Developed in the American West despite the name: a medium herder with a merle coat and endless drive.
The German service breed: herder, police dog and guide dog, 55–65 cm of steady nerve.
The short-haired Belgian herder now favoured for police and military work: fast, sharp and intense.
A miniature collie from the Shetland Isles, 33–41 cm, bred to work small sheep on poor ground.
The long-coated Scottish herder made famous by Lassie: dignified, gentle and vocal.
Short-legged Welsh cattle dog, 25–30 cm at the shoulder, once used to drive herds by nipping heels.
The shaggy drover's dog of the English west country, with a bear-like coat and a rolling gait.
